newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian privatisations on track - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italian privatisations on track - Ciampi.

text.p: Italy's privatisation programme is on track with the Treasury committed to selling off all its business holdings, Treasury Ministry Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Saturday.

Ciampi told a news conference that Italy's stop-start sell-off programme would continue as planned later this year with the already announced sale of Seat -- a publishing company controlled by state telecoms holding Stet.

He said plans for the sale of motorway operating company Autostrade were progressing, while the government intended to place a third chunk of shares in energy giant ENI on the market , "although the timetable for this still has to be established," Ciampi said.
In addition, the industry ministry was studying ways of privatising electricity utility Enel, while Stet was still firmly slated for sell-off later this year.
"It seems we have things in the works and it's our intention to proceed with alacrity," Ciampi said.
"The Treasury will be happy the day when it can call a news conference to say that it has sold everything," he added.
Privatisation plans have regularly been snarled in parliament by opponents to the sell-off programme.
Last week the government lost a vote on the transfer of Stet to Treasury control from state holding IRI after a crucial government ally, the hardleft Communist Refoundation, abstained.

The unexpected defeat heightened fears that Refoundation, which is ideologically opposed to privatisation, could effectively halt any government sell-off which requires legislation, such as the Stet placement.
